把一个项目里的每个想法都写下来、连成一张能一层层点开来读的图，再让程序盯着流程走:
Write down every idea in a project and connect them into a graph that can be read by clicking through layer by layer, then let the program monitor the process: if an idea is not clearly thought out, coding is not allowed; if tests have not failed first, implementation is not allowed; if a plan has not received a manual sign-off from a human, work is not allowed to start — the same graph is shared by three coding assistants: Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex, and it works the same way regardless of which repository it is placed in. It aims to solve the same root cause: ideas have never been written down, only code has been written down.
Starting from 2026-08-29, the three implementations that originally lived side-by-side (claude-companion, cursor-companion, codex-companion) were merged into a single common base: one engine, one guard, and three thin connection layers; the specification is written in companion/FORMAT.md, and everything is stored in a single file in ideas/graph.yaml.

The I-001~I-019 of the old graph describes that batch of code, which is no longer active code in this repository; therefore, the entire graph is reconstructed based on human decisions, with new IDs starting from I-041 (FORMAT.md stipulates that IDs are never reused).
想法节点的记录格式：每个想法必须回答八个问题: Format for recording idea nodes: every idea must answer the eight questions
一个想法节点的格式：id / name / status / needs，加上八: Format of an idea node: id / name / status / needs, plus the eight mandatory questions (what it is, why it exists, expected results, how to implement, why implement it this way, which lines the code is in, how to verify, how to use it in the future), plus an append-only log.
AI 出幻觉、prompt 对不齐需求、返工之后自己也看不懂项目框架 —— 这三: AI hallucinations, prompts not aligning with requirements, and being unable to understand the project framework after rework — the root cause of these three things is the same: ideas have never been written down, only code has been written down.
同一个想法，人和 AI 读同一份记录得到同一个理解；一个冷启动的陌生 agent: For the same idea, humans and AI read the same record to reach the same understanding; a cold-start stranger agent can continue working just by reading this file, without needing extra context.
YAML，一个扁平的 ideas 列表，一种节点、一种边。规格写在 FORMAT: YAML, a flat list of ideas, one type of node, and one type of edge. The specification is written in FORMAT.md: companion/FORMAT.md is the version shared by the three agents, and claude-companion/FORMAT.md is the version still running on the Claude side before the migration was completed; the node templates, the eight questions table, and the two ways of writing "how to verify" in both versions must match word for word. The previous statement "each of the three companions has a basically identical copy" is now obsolete: writing separately is the source of wording drift, and it is also inconsistent with the facts — Codex does not have this file at all, the Cursor version is an old version from before 2026-08-28 and lacks the entire "how to write this graph" section. Now, only the table in the common specification counts for the wording of the eight questions.
选一层扁平结构而不是需求／特性／模块／函数四层 —— FORMAT.md 结尾写: Choosing a flat structure instead of a four-layer requirement/feature/module/function structure — FORMAT.md specifies at the end: the goal is "all ideas become individual modules"; a module is not a classification method, and the four-layer structure itself is the kind of complexity that makes people unable to understand the project. YAML instead of JSON, because the eight answers are all prose paragraphs.
拿一个真实想法填一遍八问，看有没有哪个问题填不进去、或者填完还说不清这个想法: Fill in the eight questions with a real idea once to see if any question cannot be filled, or if the idea remains unclear even after filling them in.
整套工具的其它部分都只读写这一个格式；加字段的成本是一个 YAML key。\n: All other parts of the toolset only read and write this single format; the cost of adding a field is a single YAML key.
重建后的第一个节点；人工验证未签字，所以不是 done: The first node after reconstruction; manual verification has not been signed off, so it is not done.

三处过期数据已改 —— lines 143→160；how 里「三个 compa: Three instances of expired data have been corrected — lines 143→160; the "each of the three companions has a basically identical copy" in how is obsolete (actual test: Codex does not have FORMAT.md at all, the Cursor version is an old version from before 08-28 and lacks the "how to write this graph" section, while the common base version of 545 lines is not in the code of this node at all); added this note and the previous one.
人已签字：「八问够用，40 个想法都填进去了，没有填不进去的」（signed_o: Human has signed off: "The eight questions are sufficient, all 40 ideas have been filled in, with none that couldn't be filled" (signed_off recorded, original words in the log); in the same round, fixed three instances of expired data: lines 143→160, the "each of the three companions has a copy" in how is obsolete, and added two node records.
读取想法图，并检查它有没有坏掉: Read the idea graph and check if it is broken.
读 graph.yaml，检查 id 唯一、needs 指向存在的想法、图无环、: Read graph.yaml, check that IDs are unique, needs point to existing ideas, the graph has no cycles, done nodes must have code and verify, the code paths of done nodes actually exist, and manual verification must have a human sign-off; fields not filled in the eight questions are reported as warnings.
没有校验，图会安静地烂掉：done 却没有代码、code 指向已删掉的文件、两个: Without validation, the graph will quietly rot: done nodes without code, code pointing to deleted files, or two ideas depending on each other. A rotten graph is worse than no graph, because it looks complete.
健康的图 check 通过、退出码 0；每一种烂法都能被指出来并说明是哪个 id: A healthy graph passes the check and exits with code 0; every way of being rotten can be pointed out and the corresponding ID can be specified.
DFS 三色标记查环；从 endpoints 反向遍历 needs 找出通不到任: DFS three-color marking to check for cycles; reverse traverse from endpoints through needs to find orphans that do not reach any endpoint; use existsSync to verify the code paths of done nodes (todo nodes are not checked — those are planned locations).
把「done 必须有 code + verify」做成硬错误而不是警告 —— 代: Turn "done must have code + verify" into a hard error instead of a warning —— the code comments state that this is the prerequisite for the entire system to hold: if "done" can exist without evidence, this graph is merely a wish list. The code path for todo is intentionally not checked, otherwise the plan itself would be treated as an error.
/ccbuild 动手前先跑它；/ccgraph 用它的输出告诉人接下来该做什么: /ccbuild run it before taking action; /ccgraph use its output to tell people what to do next; the guard R5 uses it to block "the graph is broken at the end of a turn".
算出现在可以立刻动手做的想法有哪些: Calculate which ideas can be acted upon immediately right now
算出现在可以做哪些想法：status 是 todo、且所有前置都已 done 的: Calculate which ideas can be done now: nodes where status is todo and all prerequisites are done.
「接下来做什么」应该是图算出来的，不该是另一份要手动同步的 TODO 列表 ——: "What to do next" should be calculated by the graph, not be another TODO list that needs to be manually synchronized —— two lists will inevitably become inconsistent.
next 打出来的就是可以立刻动手的想法；一个都没有时说清是全做完了还是全被挡住: next outputs the ideas that can be acted upon immediately; when there are none, clarify whether everything is finished or everything is blocked.
一次过滤：status === todo 且 needs.every(前置已 d: Single filter: status === todo and needs.every(prerequisites are done).
不做拓扑排序 —— 代码注释写明「现在可以做什么」只需要一次过滤，做完一个再算一: Do not perform topological sort —— the code comments state that "what can be done now" only requires a single filter, recalculating after each task is completed; this reduces one potential point of failure.
/ccbuild 的入口；互不相干的、都可以立刻动手的想法可以并行交给多个 su: The entry point for /ccbuild; unrelated ideas that can all be acted upon immediately can be handed over to multiple subagents in parallel.
修改想法状态时，自动留下一条修改记录: When modifying an idea's status, automatically leave a modification record
改一个想法的状态，同时在它自己的 log 里追加一条记录；写回时保留 YAML: Change an idea's status and simultaneously append a record to its own log; preserve YAML comments when writing back; reject done without code/verify, and reject manual verification without human sign-off.
改了什么代码、什么文档、什么想法要有详细记录，而原因要放在想法旁边， 不是另一个: Detailed records must exist for what code, what documentation, and what idea was changed, while the reason must be placed next to the idea, not in another file —— if it is placed too far away, no one will read it.
set 之后重新读：状态变了、log 多了一条、原来的注释还在；对一个没有 co: Re-read after set: the status has changed, a new log entry is added, and the original comments remain; setting done for an idea without code will fail and explain the reason.
yaml 的 parseDocument 保留注释和格式，setIn 定点修改，: Use yaml's parseDocument to preserve comments and formatting, use setIn for targeted modification, write to a temporary file, and then rename.
走 Document 而不是 parse → 改 → stringify：后者会: Use Document instead of parse → modify → stringify: the latter will wipe out all comments and layout of the entire file, and comments are exactly what humans leave for themselves. rename is atomic, so a crash mid-write will not destroy the original graph (code comment: a crash mid-write leaves the old graph intact).
五个命令都通过它写状态，所以不存在「忘了记一笔」这条路径。\n: All five commands write status through it, so the path of "forgetting to record a note" does not exist.
把想法图渲染成一个可以点击、缩放的网页: Render the idea graph into a clickable, zoomable webpage
渲染成一个自包含网页：上面是只显示想法名称的完整项目图，可平移缩放； 点任意节点: Render into a self-contained webpage: at the top is a complete project graph showing only idea names, which can be panned and zoomed; click any node to jump to the detail card below, which contains all answers to the eight questions, as well as its prerequisite ideas and "which ideas it is a prerequisite for", allowing for continuous clicking in both directions.
看不见形状的项目最后一定会被重写。图是给人看的，不是给机器看的， 而人要判断的三: Projects without a visible shape will inevitably be rewritten. Graphs are for humans to look at, not for machines; the three things humans need to judge (too many nodes, missing edges, or failing to reach the endpoint) can only be judged if they are drawn.
双击打开 graph.html 就能一眼看出项目形状；缩放之后线条依然锐利； 拖: Double-click to open graph.html to see the project shape at a glance; lines remain sharp after zooming; dragging will not be misidentified as clicking a node.
Mermaid flowchart TD（CDN）做布局，节点标签只放 name: Mermaid flowchart TD (CDN) handles the layout, node labels only contain the name, and click callbacks jump to details. Zooming relies on modifying the SVG's own width/height to trigger a vector redraw, while panning relies on the wrapper's translate.
用 Mermaid 而不是 d3 / cytoscape：静态 HTML，没有构: Use Mermaid instead of d3 / cytoscape: static HTML, no build steps, and no need to start a server. Zooming deliberately avoids CSS scale() — code comments specify that scale() rasterizes the layer once before stretching, which is exactly why it previously looked blurry; fit only scales up and never down, because putting a small image at 235% is not what anyone means when they say "fit to window."
/ccthink 第 2 步用它让人在动手之前就看出拆分错了；/ccscan 用: /ccthink uses it in step 2 to let people see if the decomposition is wrong before they start working; /ccscan uses it to deliver results.
用一张文件清单证明项目真的被读完了: Use a file list to prove the project has truly been read.
/ccscan 开始时把项目里值得读的文件列成一张清单（ideas/.scan-: At the start of /ccscan, list the files worth reading in the project as a list (ideas/.scan-todo); every time a file is Read, a hook strikes it off; check continues to warn while the list is not empty. ideas/.scanignore can exclude by path prefix (third-party packages, parallel versions from other agents).
「我读完了」是一句 agent 随口就能说的话。一张图如果是从半个项目上建起来的: "I have finished reading" is a sentence an agent can say casually. If a graph is built from only half a project, it looks exactly the same as a complete one — this is worse than having no graph at all.
扫描进度是「已读 37/42」这样的数字而不是一句保证；Grep / Glob: Scanning progress is a number like "Read 37/42" rather than a mere guarantee; Grep / Glob do not count, because they do not put file content into the context.
git ls-files -z --cached --others --excl: git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard generates the list (degrades to directory traversal when git is unavailable), filtering by extension and .scanignore; strike() strikes off a line based on a case-insensitive relative path.
用 git ls-files 而不是自己遍历，因为它已经懂 .gitignore: Use git ls-files instead of manual traversal because it already understands .gitignore, submodules, and case sensitivity; -z is added because without it, git escapes non-ASCII paths into octal, making those files impossible to strike off (this is explicitly stated in the code comments). node_modules is explicitly excluded because the repository might actually have committed it.
任何声称「通读了项目」的命令都可以挂在同一张清单上。\n: Any command claiming to have "thoroughly read the project" can be attached to the same list.
七条挂在 hook 上、agent 绕不过去的强制规则: Seven mandatory rules attached to hooks that agents cannot bypass.
一个 guard.ts 挂在 PreToolUse / PostToolUse: A guard.ts is attached to PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop / UserPromptSubmit, dispatching seven rules based on events: R1 automatically logs every edit; R2 the status of an existing idea can only be changed via set; R3 implementation writing is forbidden if the test file does not exist; R4 code cannot be touched if how / why_this_way are not filled; R5 the turn cannot end if the graph has errors; R6 implementation cannot start if the graph has no human sign-off; R7 a file is only considered scanned if it has truly been Read.
五个命令都只是提示词 —— agent 可以跳过调研、编造 why_this_w: The five commands are merely prompts — an agent can skip research, fabricate why_this_way, directly Edit to change the status to done to bypass all checks, or self-answer "it looks reasonable" and continue. Discipline written in prompts becomes meaningless by the thirtieth round of dialogue.
跳过测试直接写实现会被拒绝并告诉它先写哪个文件；手改 status 会被拒绝并给: Skipping tests to write implementation will be rejected, and it will be told which file to write first; manually changing status will be rejected, and the required set command will be provided; if the graph is broken, the turn cannot end; every edit leaves a line in ideas/log.md, requiring no cooperation from the agent.
退出码 2 + stderr = 「拦下并把原因告诉 Claude」，这是四个: Exit code 2 + stderr = "intercept and tell Claude the reason"; this is the only universal mechanism across the four hook events, so a script dispatching by hook_event_name is sufficient. install.ts is responsible for writing into the target repository's .claude/settings.json without overwriting others' hooks.
只强制机器判得了的事：文件存不存在、字段填没填、状态变没变、check 过不过。: Only enforce things a machine can judge: whether a file exists, whether fields are filled, whether status has changed, and whether it passed check. The quality of eight questions or the honesty of web searches cannot be forced; the only line of defense is to make omissions visible in check and rendering — hard-blocking something that cannot be judged accurately is worse than not blocking at all. All exception paths fail open (code comment: a guard that crashes must never block work); if the guard itself crashes, it must not lock humans out; AIDEV_GUARD=off is the escape hatch.
要加新纪律就在 decide 里加一条规则加一个测试 —— 前提是它机器判得了。: If you want to add a new discipline, add a rule and a test in decide — provided that the machine can judge it.
只有人亲手输入「批准」才能生效的批准机制: An approval mechanism that only takes effect when a human manually inputs "approve".
agent 写得进去的标记，agent 就能伪造。一个「我已确认」的标记如果由被: Any marker that an agent can write, an agent can forge. If a "I have confirmed" marker is written by the constrained party themselves, it cannot constrain anything.
没批准过的图上动手会被拒绝并要求先给人看；「我不批准」不会被算成批准； 任何工具: Modifying an unapproved graph will be rejected and will require showing it to a human first; "I do not approve" will not be counted as an approval; no tool event can produce an approval.
APPROVALS 是一个集合，比对的是 trim + 小写 + 去尾部标点之后: APPROVALS is a set that compares the entire prompt after trim + lowercase + removing trailing punctuation; newline characters are normalized before hashing to prevent CRLF detection from being read as a different graph.
把「我做了」绑到一个不真做就产生不了的事件上：UserPromptSubmit: Bind "I did it" to an event that cannot be produced without actually doing it: UserPromptSubmit is only triggered when a human manually types the message. Judge "the entire message is an approval" rather than "the message contains an approval", otherwise "I do not approve" will be counted as an approval. Known ceiling (as truthfully stated in README): an agent can still use Bash to feed a fake UserPromptSubmit directly to guard.ts. R6 blocks accidental skipping, not an agent determined to bypass it.
任何「必须由人点头」的关卡都可以用同一招：绑到 agent 造不出来的事件上。\: Any checkpoint that "must be nodded by a human" can use the same trick: bind it to an event that the agent cannot create.
五个斜杠命令，覆盖从建图到实现的完整工作流: Five slash commands, covering the complete workflow from graph building to implementation.
/ccscan 通读项目建图、/ccthink 对齐→拆分→调研→设计测试→按周: /ccscan reads the entire project to build a graph, /ccthink aligns→splits→researches→designs tests→schedules weekly, /ccbuild implements with tests first, /ccfix checks if the code and idea are consistent before checking the idea itself, /ccgraph only views without modifying. Each one is a markdown prompt.
引擎只是数据结构，真正决定产出质量的是「按什么顺序做事」。 一句 prompt: The engine is just a data structure; what truly determines the quality of output is "in what order things are done". If a single prompt fails to align with requirements, the cost of rework is far higher than spending twenty minutes to align first.
每个命令在真实项目上跑一遍，产出的是它承诺的东西： /ccscan 给出诚实的覆: Run each command once on a real project; the output is what it promises: /ccscan gives honest coverage numbers and an "I don't know" list, /ccfix gives inconsistencies with line numbers instead of vague talk.
纯 markdown，步骤固定不可跳；关键处停下来等人（ccthink 第 2: Pure markdown, steps are fixed and cannot be skipped; stop at key points to wait for a human (ccthink step 2 reviews the split, ccfix step 1 reviews inconsistencies, and at the end of all commands, wait for "approval").
/ccthink 把「能借就借」设成命令里优先级最高的规则，并把调研放在回答 「: /ccthink sets "borrow whenever possible" as the highest priority rule in the command, and places research before answering "how to implement" — otherwise, research will only become a way to find justification for existing answers. /ccfix deliberately does not let the AI judge whether the code or the idea is correct: it is precisely the party that cannot judge. /ccscan explicitly prohibits fabricating why_this_way, because fabricated reasons will be treated as facts by the next agent and maintained indefinitely, which is the greatest harm this command can cause.
五个命令各在一个真实项目上跑一遍，确认每一步都做到了它承诺的事；尤其看 /ccf: Run each of the five commands once on a real project to confirm every step achieves what it promises; especially check if /ccfix reports accurate line numbers.
产出的图直接就是 /ccbuild 的执行计划，中间不需要再转一次格式。\n: The produced graph is directly the execution plan for /ccbuild, with no need for an intermediate format conversion.
五个命令都写完并装出去了，但没有一个在真项目上从头到尾走过；人工验证未签字: All five commands are written and installed, but none have been walked through from start to finish on a real project; manual verification has not been signed off.
2026-09-06 的全仓库文字排查（I-118）查出两处技能正文说得和引擎不: Full repository text inspection on 2026-09-06 (I-118) found two places where the skill body text differs from the engine, because these two files are claimed by this item and should be absorbed by this item rather than I-118: 1. ccbuild lines 32–34 say "when entering doing, supplement whatever is missing", missing the fourth condition — this idea's currently valid plan approval (ideas.ts's setStatus checks it when entering doing), and writing test files also requires the same approval; 2. ccgraph line 32 says "blocked ideas are each waiting for something, status has the answer", but status only provides notes for todo and doing, while blocked ones only provide numbers and names. To fix these two places, either follow the approval process of this item, or absorb this item first and then establish a new idea.
用文件名后缀区分不同 agent，各写各的文件: Distinguish different agents using file name suffixes, so each writes its own files.
ideas/graph.yaml 空着就用它并在文件里写 agent: clau: If ideas/graph.yaml is empty, use it and write agent: claude in the file; if it is taken by someone else, use ideas/graph.claude.yaml. Add the corresponding .approved / .scan-todo / log.md suffixes together. Once chosen, keep it fixed, because the fact that "the file with the suffix already exists" is itself the answer.
Claude、Codex、Cursor 三个 companion 住在同一个仓库: Three companions—Claude, Codex, and Cursor—reside in the same repository and all want ideas/graph.yaml. Whoever writes later will destroy the previous one.
三边并存，谁也不覆盖谁；一个没有 agent: 键的 graph.yaml 被当: Three sides coexist without overwriting each other; a graph.yaml without an agent: key is treated as belonging to someone else (assuming the reverse would destroy others' work).
nameIsTaken 先看带后缀的文件在不在（在 = 已经选过了），再看不带后: For nameIsTaken, first check if the file with the suffix exists (exists = already selected), then check the agent: line in the file without the suffix; for agentName, determine whether the suffix is inserted or appended based on whether an extension exists (dotfiles have no extension to split).
先到的保留干净名字。用「文件是否存在」当状态，而不是另存一份配置 —— 少一个可: The first to arrive keeps the clean name. Use "file existence" as the state instead of saving a separate configuration—this reduces the number of places where reality might become inconsistent. The agent: key is not decoration; code comments state that without it, the next call will misidentify our own suffix-less graph as someone else's, thereby quietly switching to the file with the suffix and discarding the graph we just wrote.
再加第四个 agent 只需要换一个 AGENT 常量。\n: Adding a fourth agent only requires changing one AGENT constant.
把这套工作流安装进其它仓库: Install this workflow into other repositories.
把五个命令复制进目标仓库的 .claude/commands/（路径改写成绝对路: Copy the five commands into the target repository's .claude/commands/ (rewrite the path to an absolute path), create an empty ideas/graph.yaml, attach the guard to the four events in .claude/settings.json, and write a ideas/.gitignore to distinguish "records that should enter git" from "local machine state."
这套流程要用在所有项目上，不是只用在这一个仓库里。\n: This process must be used on all projects, not just in this single repository.
在别的仓库里五个斜杠命令都能调起来；不覆盖已经存在的、不属于这套工具的 命令文件: In other repositories, all five slash commands can be invoked; do not overwrite existing command files that do not belong to this tool (unless using --force); repeated installations result in no change, and hooks will not pile up indefinitely.
逐个复制 commands/*.md 并把 `claude-companion/: Copy commands/*.md one by one and replace `claude-companion/` with the absolute path of the current directory; when installing hooks, filter out your own old one before adding it back, while keeping others exactly as they are.
引擎（ideas.ts / guard.ts）刻意不复制 —— 所有仓库共用一份: The engine (ideas.ts / guard.ts) is intentionally not copied—all repositories share one copy, so fixing it once fixes it everywhere, preventing five repositories from running five different versions. The cost is that if this directory is moved, it needs to be reinstalled. graph and log.md go into git (as they are records), while .scan-todo and .approved do not (a partial scan and a human sign-off are local machine states).
在一个真实的、不是这个仓库的项目上装好，重启 Claude Code，确认五个命: Install it on a real project that is not this repository, restart Claude Code, and confirm that the five commands can be invoked and the hook actually blocks actions.
新项目的第一步：装上，跑 /ccscan。\n: The first step for a new project: install it, then run /ccscan.
记录装到了哪些仓库，并能检查是否过期、批量更新: Record which repositories are installed, and be able to check if they are expired and perform batch updates.

本次 /ccscan 亲眼撞上了：同一轮里并行 Read 五个文件，hook 也: This /ccscan personally encountered it: during the same round, five files were read in parallel, which meant the hook also ran five guard processes in parallel, each performing readWorklist → filter → writeFileSync. The later write overwrote the earlier write, leaving evidence in the log ("Read .gitignore (32 remaining)" immediately followed by "Read package.json (32 remaining)", the number did not decrease), and a line of incomplete content `n` was written into the list. The result was: the files were indeed read, but the ledger said they were not read — the number reported by R7 actually became inaccurate.
并行 Read N 个文件之后，清单恰好少 N 行，且不出现任何不是文件路径的行: After reading N files in parallel, the list should be exactly N lines short, and no lines other than file paths should appear.
让 strike 不再重写清单，改成只追加，race 就不存在了。 .scan-: Make strike no longer rewrite the list, but change it to append only, so that race conditions no longer exist. .scan-todo becomes a list written only once (generated by scan, which is truly a single process); add a new append-only .scan-done, where strike finishes after appending one line using appendFileSync, without reading, modifying, or rewriting anything; "what remains" becomes the set difference of "list minus already read," so duplicate appending is harmless, and a torn half-line will simply not match anything. Appending must be a single write call (passing a pre-constructed full string, without using WriteStream or multiple calls), otherwise atomicity is not established. Change the return value of strike from true/false to the remaining count in its own snapshot, so that the guard does not need to read a second time when logging — otherwise, the symptom "two consecutive writes both say 7 remaining" will still appear after the fix. The contract of the return value must be able to distinguish two things, otherwise it will silently corrupt R7: if not in the list, or if no scan is running, return -1; if truly struck out, return the remaining count of this snapshot (which can be 0). Raw numbers cannot achieve this — "not in the list" and "struck out with 0 remaining" would both be 0, and guard.ts currently branches based on truthy/falsy values (`if (!struck) return OK`), and the two existing green tests happen to cover these two directions: one asserts that no log is recorded when there is no list, and one asserts that when striking out the last one, it must log "0 remaining in scan." Change the fixed temporary filename ${file}.tmp in save to a name with a process ID and a random suffix (copying the codex implementation), and add EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES retry to rename: renaming to overwrite an existing file is unreliable on Windows. .scan-done must be added to both the guard's write-protection list and ideas/.gitignore, otherwise an agent could write its own "I have read it," which is the entire reason R7 exists. Finally, perform a one-time migration for scan: list = the current project file list, already read = list minus the old remaining, and the already read items must be reconciled with the list, discarding anything that is not a known path in the list — the incomplete line `n` currently stuck in the list will therefore automatically disappear.
原来写的「对齐 save 的临时文件 + rename」只是半个修复，而这个仓库: The original implementation of "align save temporary file + rename" was only a half-fix, and this repository provides immediate counter-evidence: rename makes "writing" atomic, but it does not serialize "reading". strike reads first, then writes; another process may have already read the old list in the interim, so when it writes back, it overwrites the results of others. The evidence is in lines 301 and 302 of ideas/log.claude.md — both lines write "7 remaining scanned", yet the file that was supposedly struck out remains the first line of the list to this day. The command_reviewed on the codex side is a more advanced version of the same error: it uses correct atomic writes, but it is still "read-modify-write", which still results in lost writes. Even the most complete of the three implementations failed here. Changing to append-only resolves both symptoms simultaneously: the operating system handles positioning for each append, N concurrent processes produce N complete records, and no locks, retries, waiting, or any new dependencies are required. This also holds true on Windows: the underlying library adds FILE_APPEND_DATA to append mode, which is the Windows equivalent of the POSIX semantics. I must clarify the boundaries of this evidence to avoid overstating: guard uses append for logging, and in log.claude.md, there are only three moments that truly prove "simultaneous writing" (the remaining count 32 appears three times, 19 twice, and 7 twice); the other hundreds of lines were written sequentially and do not prove concurrency. Therefore, the real guarantee is not "we tried many times and it didn't break," but rather "the growth of file length is atomic, and the upper limit for non-interleaved content is the disk sector size (512B to 4KB), while each of our records is a path of only a few dozen bytes." The first step of implementation is to measure this — first write the concurrency test, run it against the current code to confirm it actually fails (red), and then modify the implementation. Additionally, I am noting a more thorough approach that was considered but not adopted this round: Claude Code has a PostToolBatch event, which triggers only once after an entire batch of parallel tool calls has finished. Moving the strike action there would mean only one process is writing, eliminating concurrency at the source, which is simpler than any concurrency-safe implementation. The reason for not adopting it is that it would require modifying the installer to register a new event, depend on newer versions, and it would change the semantics of R7 itself (striking out by batch rather than by each Read), which is a matter for FORMAT.md to adjudicate, not something a bug fix should handle casually. The append-only approach does not conflict with it: regardless of which event triggers it, the writing method is safe, and it remains valid for the uncapped concurrency brought by sub-agents. No locks: approximately thirty lines of code would be exchanged for three new ways to fail, and stale locks are a long-term cost rather than an edge case — hook processes can be killed by the outer layer, and locks often outlive the processes. By design, guard must "allow through on error," so every lock path would need a "give up striking on timeout" branch, which would effectively reintroduce undercounting, and undercounting is exactly what R7 aims to eliminate. Node also lacks a built-in file lock to fall back on. No third-party packages: this engine has the design prerequisite that "installing in other repositories requires nothing," and since guard starts a new process for every Read, every dependency incurs a cost on every tool call. More directly, those atomic write packages only serialize writes within a single process, whereas the five writers here are in five separate processes; they do not solve the fundamental problem. Lock packages have not been maintained for years and have documented failure loops on Windows. The common foundation D30 has already ruled on this divergence: all generated state atomic writes must use process locks or single atomic appends for append logs. Known boundaries, written here to avoid being treated as a bug later: append atomicity does not hold on network drives; it is only safe on local disks when a single line is much smaller than a sector — here we store file paths, which is more than enough.

先说为什么是「删」而不是「关掉」：Claude Code 没有关闭单条 hook: First, why "delete" instead of "disable": Claude Code does not have a switch to disable individual hooks; the only switch would disable all hooks together, including the guard itself; and the hooks in settings.local.json are additive and merged, with no syntax to "negate a specific item from a previous layer." Therefore, deletion is the only way to avoid accidentally harming the guard. Second, why not just implement an uninstallation feature: the D14 of the common base has already adjudicated the scope of responsibility for install.ts — local development, old installation migration, and viewing/refreshing installed repositories; formal distribution and uninstallation are handled by each agent's own plugin layer. Creating an uninstallation subcommand now would be equivalent to building something that the common base has explicitly decided not to own. In the history of this repository, there actually was an uninstallation script (in the parent commit of ca7e956); its approach was to filter out its own entries based on characteristic substrings in the commands, and then remove the resulting empty groups — which is also the standard solution across the entire ecosystem. However, it relies on a different registry format and several files that no longer exist; bringing the whole thing back would be the kind of scope expansion that was rejected. When actually implemented, it would be a dozen lines of inversion of the four lines of filtering logic in installHooks, not something new. Finally, why a manual deletion read by a human instead of creating a new mechanism: the commit message for ca7e956 explicitly states "also deleted references interrupted by the archiving action: pointing to the hook in packages/hook/dist," and the change to settings.json in that commit only rearranged those two items from single lines into indented JSON, without deleting a single one. The reason is that the installHooks filter only recognizes its own command names, so it cannot structurally delete others'. This file has already been fooled once by an automatic fix that "looked successful"; we shouldn't let it happen a second time. There is also one risk that must be stated: this is the agent modifying the file that "decides whether the agent is managed." Cursor's specification directly prohibits this (it lists hook configuration as a locked file, with the reason being that agents are not allowed to uninstall their own constraints), whereas the common base's D24 did not put hook configuration on the protection list. The mitigation is for a human to read the changes before committing.

This is the literal meaning of "sorting by ID within the same layer"—depth comes first, ID comes second; it is neither a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) queue nor a greedy approach that takes the minimum at each step (both of those would move an idea from the second layer ahead of an idea from the first layer that has not yet been output). After finishing, take the nodes whose in-degree is still greater than zero (i.e., those in a cycle), sort them by ID, and append them to the end, losing none. The three orders look very similar, and a three-node linear fixture cannot distinguish them, so the tests must use the following two small graphs (I have run all three implementations, and the numbers are actual outputs, not conjectures): I. I-002 needs I-001, I-004 needs I-003 — both layer-by-layer and FIFO give I-001, I-003, I-002, I-004, while taking the minimum at each step gives I-001, I-002, I-003, I-004. This fixture catches "copying codex." Both are required; having only one would allow the other incorrect implementation to pass. The return value is the idea objects themselves, accessed by array index without going through the ID lookup table: the lookup table only keeps the last entry for duplicate IDs, and the command-line `render` never runs `check` first, so duplicate IDs would cause a card to vanish into thin air. Do not modify the existing `findCycle`.

Borrow its shape, but the queue must be replaced: it uses FIFO (sorting only at the initial seed and each expansion), which is neither "sorting by ID within the same layer" nor "taking the minimum at each step"—the three orders are distinct, and copying it will result in the third type. This point is explicitly required by `expected`, so it must be decided and clearly documented. I choose layer-by-layer because its sole consumer, I-061, requires exactly this: "Cards are arranged from the foundation with no prerequisites all the way to the end"—read all ideas without prerequisites first, then read those built upon them. Taking the minimum at each step cannot achieve this: it would output an idea from the second layer with a smaller ID before an idea from the first layer has been output. Why not merge with `findCycle`: it breaks the entire traversal when it encounters the first cycle, and merging would return a truncated order, losing nodes—whereas "not losing nodes" is exactly what `expected` forbids violating. Furthermore, the required return values differ: `check` prints the path of the cycle (which only depth-first can provide), while `topoOrder` requires the complete sequence. `findCycle` is code already completed by someone else (I-042). Current IDs are three-digit numbers with zero-padding, so character order happens to equal numerical order; a project using a mix of one-digit and two-digit IDs would sort in reverse. I ran a function of the same shape with real tsx, evaluated the injection result, and it reported __name is undefined. What is even more fatal is that it cannot be caught: the transformation suite used for running tests does not depend on esbuild, so tests will all be green, while the page opened by double-clicking will error out directly. A failure mode that a test can never discover should not be chosen. Remediation is not impossible — write a __name shim before injection and add a test that actually spawns a child process to watch it — but that would be to preserve a mechanism that provides no benefit here, adding two new things out of thin air. Since the page generation script is already hand-written using template strings (as is already done in this file), writing the function body as a string constant involves zero extra mechanisms. The cost must be stated clearly: the string constant version loses type checking. Therefore, that test of "identical character-for-character output on both sides" is not just a bonus; it is the safety net for this decision, and without it, this choice is invalid.

Connecting and disconnecting edges are written as a pair of "from which to which," rather than a new value for the entire prerequisite list. An envelope wraps the entire sequence of operations: format version number, project path, and the embedded image fingerprint from the page — the fingerprint is brought back exactly as is; the page never calculates it itself. Incidentally, this fixes an existing adjacency defect: when a draft is written, the fingerprint is stored, but when it is read back, it is never compared, meaning a draft written against an old image would be silently restored. This sentence must be written in the node, because it is precisely the difference between "two lines of changes" and "one new module," and it is also the reason why the original sentence "make deletion a mark for deletion" sounded trivial. 计数器写成图文件顶层的一个字段，只由会发编号的命令递增，任何其它地方只读。 **: The counter is written as a field at the top level of the graph file, incremented only by the command that issues IDs; any other place is read-only. **The initial value is written as a rule, not as a number**: when the field does not yet exist in the graph, calculate it once as "the maximum ID that has appeared in this graph + 1" and write it in. The original text "the maximum ID is I-075, so the initial value is 76" is now obsolete — when that sentence was written, the graph had not yet grown to I-080; initializing according to 76 would cause I-076 to I-080 to be reissued, which is exactly what this field is meant to prevent. A hardcoded number will inevitably expire as long as the graph continues to grow. The specification clearly states two hard rules: the web page only issues temporary IDs; real IDs are issued all at once during write-back and all temporary IDs are replaced, and if replacement is incomplete, the entire write-back is rejected. The format of the change file is written out item by item according to the envelope and the six operations, with one example for each.
计数器放进图文件而不是让网页算：编号永不复用是格式规定，而被删掉的编号页面根本看: Put the counter in the graph file instead of letting the web page calculate it: ID non-reuse is a format rule, and the web page cannot see deleted IDs at all. Incidentally, correct an erroneous reason previously written in the graph — the original text said "old graph I-001~I-040 has been retired, and the page calculating max based on the current graph will collide with them," which is wrong: the living IDs are I-041~I-075, and max+1 yields I-076, which does not collide with any retired IDs. The real vulnerability occurs after deletion: if the idea with the largest ID is deleted, max retreats, and the next creation obtains the ID that was just deleted. Two web pages calculating the same ID simultaneously is a concurrent version of the same bug — this is also why Rails abandoned sequential ID migration years ago. The two matters are combined into one node because they are two halves of the same thing: both are "new things added to this pipeline that must be searchable in the specification," and both involve modifying the same managed file. Splitting them into two nodes would cause the same specification to be approved twice.

If only text can be modified and not the structure, these two types of high-value modifications must still loop back to the YAML file.

四件事，都落在生成网页的那个函数里。 **前置箭头**：每张卡片的「前置想法」从: Four tasks, all falling within the function that generates the webpage. **Prerequisite arrows**: The "prerequisite idea" of each card changes from a read-only link to an editable one — a dropdown menu to select an existing idea to connect to, with an 'X' next to each connected arrow to disconnect it. Each operation appends a "connect" or "disconnect" entry to the ledger, writing "from which to which," rather than the new value of the entire prerequisite list. **New**: A "Create New Idea" button that produces an empty card with a temporary ID; it cannot enter the submission stage if the first three questions (What, Why, Expected Result) are not fully filled. **Delete**: A "Delete" button on the card that performs a "mark for deletion," which can be undone, and only becomes a deletion operation upon submission. **Redraw**: As soon as the structure changes, call the shared drawing function to recalculate the graph source, then create a brand-new graph element to replace the old one — the drawing library stamps processed elements, so changing text in place will not trigger a redraw. All text must be assigned using textContent. Redrawing must preserve the user's current zoom and pan; the view cannot reset to the full graph every time a change is made. This cross-module section requires two changes: move the editing script before the drawing script (it is currently reversed, meaning editing is initialized only after a cross-network module fetch); the drawing section must attach a redraw function externally after its own dependencies are loaded, following the current "click node to jump to card" approach — that is the only bridge between these two scripts today. The editing script should only perform feature detection and must never wait. **Offline**: When the redraw function cannot be detected, adding, deleting, and submitting work as usual, the page explicitly states "Graph temporarily unavailable (offline)," and the original graph source text must be hidden — currently, if drawing fails, the reader sees a screen full of flowchart source code. Prerequisite links on cards remain clickable because they are actual anchor links.

网页上有一个「提交」动作，把人这一次做的全部改动（改文字、改状态、新建删除想法、: There is a "Submit" action on the webpage that packages all changes made this time (modifying text, modifying status, creating/deleting ideas, adding/deleting prerequisite relationships) into a change record to be sent out. The page first probes whether a local server exists: if yes, it sends it directly to be saved by the server; if no (for example, if the file was opened by double-clicking), it falls back to downloading it as a file and explicitly tells the user where to put it.
浏览器里的网页写不了项目里的文件 —— 这是整条链路里唯一跨不过去的墙。本地服务: Webpages in a browser cannot write to files in the project — this is the only insurmountable wall in the entire chain. A local server is the main gate to cross this wall, and downloading is the backup gate when there is no server. The two paths must deliver the exact same thing, otherwise the write-back end would have to recognize two different formats.
有服务器的时候：点「提交」→ 页面列出逐条改动 → 人点确认 → 改动落进图，页: When a server is present: Click "Submit" → the page lists changes one by one → user clicks confirm → changes are applied to the graph, and the page displays the new graph, without touching the file system throughout the process. When no server is present: Click "Submit" → receive a change file, along with the instruction "Put it in <absolute path>, then run this command." In both cases, the button is unclickable if nothing has been changed.
探测就是对服务器的健康检查地址发一次请求，超时设得很短，失败就当没有 —— 探测: Probing is sending a request to the server's health check address; the timeout is set very short, and a failure is treated as non-existence — a failed probe must never cause the page to freeze or trigger an error. **With a server**: Send the ledger envelope (containing the image fingerprint and a one-time token in the page) to the server; the server first returns a line-by-line comparison of changes for human confirmation, and the changes are only truly committed to disk after the human clicks confirm; upon success, the page redraws using the new image returned by the server and clears the ledger. **Without a server**: Serialize the same envelope into text and follow a two-level fallback — first, attempt to trigger a download (wrap the text into a temporary object, create a temporary link, click it, and defer garbage collection); if that fails, display a text box that allows for select-all and copying; in both cases, simultaneously display the absolute path of ideas/ (embedded in the page during rendering) and the specific command to be run. Upon successful submission, do not clear the draft, only mark it as "submitted" — wait until the changes have actually landed in the image before allowing a human to discard them.
服务器优先而不是永远走文件：人的原话是「不好同步」，而中间插一个需要手动搬运的文: Prioritize the server rather than always using files: the person's original words were "hard to sync," and inserting a file that requires manual moving is exactly what causes the lack of synchronization. The fallback is retained because the version opened by direct double-clicking must also be able to submit — the same code, one feature probe, and one fallback branch incur very low cost, in exchange for ensuring this webpage can still be entered into git, sent to others, and opened on machines without Node installed. **Reject showSaveFilePicker as the first level**: The original text stated "tested and usable under file://," but the first step in the specification for "checking if the current environment allows popping up a file picker" rejects opaque origins; file:// documents are indeed opaque origins, and three independent investigations point to this conclusion. That manual test was likely performed in a different context. It is not treated as the first level because a path that works intermittently would cause the other two levels to never see real usage and thus never be verified. If re-testing confirms it truly works in your browser, it can be an added bonus as "use it if detected," but it cannot be written as a promise. **The final level must be a text box rather than the clipboard**: The clipboard interface is also frequently unavailable under file://, whereas a text box that allows select-all will not fail in any browser — the sole requirement for the fallback level is that it must not fail. Each change carries the old value to allow the write-back end to perform line-by-line comparison and conflict display: a change record that only carries the new value can only be discarded entirely if a conflict is encountered. Do not clear the draft upon success: if the write-back is rejected (e.g., the image was modified by another session during editing — this actually occurred once on the day of the investigation), the human's changes must not be lost entirely.
改动记录是网页和写回那端之间的唯一接口；将来换一种编辑界面，只要产出同样的信封就: The change record is the sole interface between the webpage and the write-back end; in the future, if the editing interface is changed, as long as it produces the same envelope, it can connect to the same pipeline.

引擎新增一个子命令：读改动文件，把每一处修改写进 ideas/graph.cla: The engine adds a new subcommand: read the change file and write every modification into ideas/graph.claude.yaml — text changes are written to specific points, status changes follow the existing "set + automatic record keeping" logic, and the creation/deletion of ideas and edges is executed according to format rules; after writing, it automatically validates and re-renders the webpage, and changes are recorded in the record file.
写回如果靠 agent 手工编辑 YAML，注释会被抹掉、状态可能绕过 set、: If write-back relies on an agent manually editing YAML, comments will be erased, status might bypass the set logic, and the format might be corrupted — these are exactly the things this tool was intended to prevent. Write-back must be a deterministic command, not an act of free improvisation.
对一个带注释的图应用改动文件之后：每处改动都生效，注释和没动过的部分逐字保留，: After applying a change file to an image with comments: every change takes effect, comments and untouched parts are preserved verbatim, validation passes, corresponding entries are added to the record file, and the webpage has been re-rendered; applying the same change file a second time will not produce any further changes.
引擎新增 apply 子命令，核心是一个可单独测试的纯函数：读改动文件 → 在内: The engine adds a new `apply` subcommand, which is core-wise a pure function that can be tested independently: Read change file → Apply all changes in memory and run a full check; if any step fails, the entire operation is abandoned and the disk remains untouched → only then perform an atomic write to disk, re-render, and record logs. Key points: If `baseDigest` does not equal the current idea graph fingerprint, the entire operation is rejected (optimistic lock); operations are sorted by "modify fields first, then delete nodes"; after each structural operation, the in-memory snapshot is rebuilt—otherwise, writing according to old indices will cause the state to fall onto the wrong idea (this silent pollution was verified through adversarial testing); state operations are redirected to the existing `setStatus` evidence verification, and the explanatory text is also pulled from there into the log to avoid duplicate recording; new operations force the status to `todo` and strip the `log` and `human sign-off` fields from the payload—otherwise, a change file could spontaneously create "completed and signed-off" ideas; delete operations require that no other ideas depend on it, and the section comments attached to the deleted node are moved to the next node; new nodes use `doc.createNode` and set the loose text fields to a block-folding style (otherwise, shoving raw objects into a YAML document makes them unchangeable later, as verified); any completed idea whose behavior fields (`what` / `expected` / `how` / `why_this_way` / `verify`) have been modified will automatically be downgraded to `doing` and a log will be left—ensuring the three rules of "test first, think clearly, and human approval" re-apply to it. Upon success, rename the change file to `changes.applied-<date>.json`, and the end of the output will include a fixed reminder to "refresh the browser page before starting the next round"; the `set` subcommand also performs a re-render after writing to disk to ensure the web pages on disk are always fresh. **ID issuance is unified here**: Temporary IDs from the page are all replaced with real IDs in one go before application (taken from the ID counter, incrementing by one for each), and places referencing temporary IDs in prerequisite relationships are synchronized; if any temporary IDs remain after replacement, the entire write to disk is rejected. **Three ways to preserve the diff, all measured on a real graph; missing any one will turn a change into a full-file reordering**: 1. When converting the document back to text, no parameters can be passed — passing the "no line wrap" option will reorder all folded paragraphs; verified on this graph, it would move 1274/1301 lines and shorten the file by 291 lines; passing no parameters results in byte-for-byte identity. 2. When writing prerequisite relationships, a node must first be created and then marked with a single-line style; directly inserting a regular array will turn the single-line `needs: [ I-042 ]` into a three-line list, verified to move 444 lines; marking the style only moves 1 line. 3. If the deleted item is the **first** idea, that section title is not attached to it, but to the entire idea sequence — merely moving the "deleted node's comments" will orphan the title onto the new first node. This point requires its own test.
写回必须是确定性指令而不是 agent 自由发挥——注释、格式、校验都会在自由发: Writing back must be a deterministic instruction rather than agent free-play — comments, formatting, and verification will all be lost in free-play. All verification is built into the engine rather than relying on hooks: `apply` runs via Bash, and hooks cannot see it at all. This trust boundary must be honestly stated: `apply` guards "state has evidence, the graph is not corrupted, and changes are recorded," but it does not guard "changes must come from a human" (that is the responsibility of I-066). Here, I must also retract a previous overstatement: the original text said "state operations are redirected to the existing `setStatus` evidence verification," but `setStatus` on the Claude side actually only blocks two things: "missing code/verify in `done`" and "missing `human verification` sign-off" — it does not check if the eight questions are complete, does not check if prerequisites are finished, and does not check approval. The Cursor version is the one that truly gates by readiness; this discrepancy has already been noted in the specification. Therefore, the honest statement is: reusing `setStatus` for state operations is to ensure there is only one entry point for logs and to inherit its two checks; it is not "inheriting a full set of readiness verifications." To be stricter, `setStatus` itself must be strengthened, which is another idea. Writing back does not borrow existing patch libraries: research showed a package specifically for "modifying YAML via patches while preserving comments," but it itself is built on top of the same YAML library plus a patch library — and this engine already has that YAML library and the load/save read/write functions. I have verified on a real 50,352-byte graph: parsing and converting back to text results in byte-for-byte identity. In other words, this hardest constraint is obtained for free; installing that package would just be asking for something we already have, while adding a failure mode of "patch fails if the difference is too large" — and here, fuzzy matching is not needed at all; IDs are precise addresses. `check` is moved before writing to disk because the bottom line of this toolset is that bad graphs are not written to disk; "automatic downgrade of completed ideas" is the minimal fix for the largest process loophole discovered during adversarial testing — the `guard` would otherwise allow the code file of a completed idea to pass through directly, and if not downgraded, the code could be changed without approval after the graph is modified. The change format does not borrow JSON Patch (RFC 6902, which uses indices and does not recognize IDs) nor JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396, where arrays can only be replaced entirely): preserving comments requires the application side to iterate through the YAML Document interface item by item; any existing patch library application engine would be extremely heavy; we use a custom operation list by ID, aligning semantically with the precedent of Kubernetes strategic merge patch's `merge-by-key`.
agent 对齐代码之前跑的就是这条指令；它也是以后任何「机器改图」场景的唯一入: This is the command the agent runs before aligning code; it is also the sole entry point for any future "machine-modifies-graph" scenarios.

All 12 tests are green; browser testing: edit toggle, dirty markers, reverting to original values to cancel markers, degrading to pure memory when storage is unavailable, and draft recovery/discarding taking effect item-by-item.
改动记账本：六种操作的有序清单 + 信封（版本/项目/图指纹），草稿和磁盘文件同: Modified the ledger: an ordered list of six operations + envelope (version/project/graph fingerprint), with drafts and disk files sharing the same format; createLedger is implemented as a shared source code string, so the engine and the page evaluate the same text; the page's editing script is redirected to this ledger, drafts are stored in envelopes, and the previously stored but never compared fingerprint expiration check has been added. test_change_envelope.test.ts: 15 tests went from red to green + 2 page wiring assertions (added later, not initially red).
编号为什么只发临时号：真编号必须由写回时统一发放，理由写在取号计数器那个想法里，: Why are only temporary IDs issued: real IDs must be issued uniformly during write-back; the reason is written in the idea regarding the ID counter, and this only uses it. The benefit is that this idea can start working without waiting for the format specification to be finalized. Why are edges recorded as a pair of "connected/disconnected" instead of a new value for the entire list: the ledger idea has already ruled that two edge changes on the same idea cannot overwrite each other. Why move the editing script forward: testing shows that the current editing section is placed after the drawing section, and the first thing the drawing section does is fetch modules from the CDN and uses top-level await — meaning today's editing functionality is initialized only after a cross-network request. Moving the position has zero cost, and the benefit is that editing is immediately available during network outages. Why use a global function as a bridge instead of an event bus or shared module: a bridge already exists (clicking a node jumps to a card); adding another function capable of feature detection is shorter than introducing an event mechanism and provides one less way to fail than importing another module under file://. Why redrawing must create new elements: the drawing library stamps processed elements, so in-place modification will not take effect — this is a pitfall that makes people think "redrawing wasn't triggered" and leads them to modify other things randomly. Why preserve zoom and pan: if a person is staring at a corner of the graph to modify something, and every redraw jumps back to the full view, the feature becomes unusable. Why hide source code during network outages: this is an existing defect (drawing failure = source code all over the screen); after adding redrawing, it will be encountered more frequently, so fixing it while at it is cheaper than opening a new idea. Why nodes and edges are no longer split into two ideas: they use the same machinery — the same ledger, the same redraw path, and the same shared function; splitting them would result in two almost identical nodes and two almost identical tests. The benefit of splitting is "being able to verify them separately," but here, the two sets of assertions in the same test file can verify them separately.
新增 apply 子命令（引擎的第八个词）：纯函数 applyChanges 收: Added the apply subcommand (the engine's eighth word): a pure function applyChanges takes graph text + envelope and returns new text or a reason for rejection, without touching the disk; the flow is Version → Fingerprint → Four stages (new/field status/edge/deletion) → Full graph validation → then disk write. Three ways to ensure diffs are implemented and each has tests: converting text without parameters, needs using createNode+flow, and attaching section headers to the sequence when deleting the first idea. Temporary IDs are issued uniformly, and if only one remains, it is rejected; new ideas are forced to todo and stripped of status/records/sign-off; if a completed idea is modified, its field automatically reverts to doing. test_ideas_apply.test.ts: 20 tests went from red to green + end-to-end execution (new idea receives I-081, next_id lands next to endpoints, modified files are archived, page re-renders).
本地小服务：当场把想法图渲染给浏览器，并接住浏览器发回来的改动: Local small service: renders the idea graph to the browser on the spot and catches the changes sent back by the browser.
引擎新增一个子命令，启动一个只监听本机的小服务：当场把当前的图渲染成网页送给浏览: The engine adds a subcommand that starts a small service listening only to the local machine: it renders the current graph as a webpage to the browser on the spot, catches the change records sent back by the browser, returns an item-by-item comparison for human confirmation first, calls the write-back logic to save to disk after human confirmation, and then sends the new graph back to the page. It ends when the human closes it.
浏览器里的网页写不了磁盘，所以改完之后要人手动搬一个文件、再敲一条指令 —— 这: Webpages in the browser cannot write to the disk, so after modifying, a person must manually move a file and then type a command — this is the most awkward part of the entire chain and the true source of "difficulty in syncing modified graphs." A local small service can turn this part into "save with one click." It also fixes another persistent problem: the webpage on the disk is generated and will expire; in service mode, that file does not exist at all, and what is seen is always the current graph.
跑起来之后浏览器能打开图；在页面上改一处、提交，图文件真的变了，而且页面上显示的: Once running, the browser can open the graph; modify one place on the page and submit, the graph file truly changes, and the page displays the new graph after the modification; if the graph was modified by another session during this period, it is rejected entirely with a clear reason; the service only accepts requests from the local machine, and write operations must include the token generated during this startup.
用 Node 自带的 http 模块，不引任何框架。只绑本机回环地址，不是绑到所: Uses Node's built-in http module without importing any frameworks. It only binds to the local loopback address, not to all network cards. A one-time token is generated at startup and only written into the webpage being rendered on the spot; any write operation without the correct token is rejected. Three paths: one returns the currently rendered page, one is a health check (for the page to detect if the service is running), and one receives changes. The receiving path has two steps: first, calculate without writing and return the item-by-item comparison to the page; once the human clicks confirm, call the write-back logic with the same record. The reply uses the same apply core and never writes a separate one — so fingerprint validation, preventing bad graphs from being written to disk, and logging all proceed as before. A default port is provided, and if occupied, it increments; the final address is printed and an attempt is made to open the browser. It ends when the human presses Ctrl-C or closes the window.
这是这类工具的行业标准形状（本地内容管理工具的 local backend 就是: This is the industry standard shape for this type of tool (this is how the local backend of local content management tools works). In my initial research, I rejected it because I thought it "would break double-click-to-use" — but what people want is exactly that "double-click-to-use service," so that reason no longer holds; I am recording this here truthfully. Use Node's built-in http instead of any framework: there are only three routes, and a framework is pure overhead; furthermore, the design premise of this engine is that it requires no additional installation when added to other repositories. **为什么是「每个想法写一个上级」，而不是再加一种箭头。** 这份记录里前后关系:
**Why is it "one parent per idea" instead of adding another type of arrow?** In this record, "prerequisite" is the only relationship. Adding a second type of arrow would mean every time a reader sees a line, they have to ask what kind it is. Ownership only answers one question: under whom does this idea belong. It does not participate in "who must finish first," so an idea can still be a prerequisite for an idea on another branch; the page renders that prerequisite as a cross-page link. If this point is ambiguous, layering will be mistaken for a new sequence of precedence, and someone will attempt to schedule project timelines based on it.
**Why replace the entire flat step-by-step overview with a tree instead of adding a layer to it?** There are three concrete reasons. First, a flat layout is inherently single-layered: its shape is "a sequential table at the top of the file + one tag per idea." To add a second layer, you would need another table and another tag, and both tables would each require maintaining their own order; a tree uses only one field to support arbitrary layers. Second, "steps" are a second type of thing that appears out of thin air: they are not ideas, they cannot be depended upon by other ideas, they have no status, and they do not have their own page. After changing to a tree, a "step" becomes just an ordinary idea—answering the eight questions, following the status flow, and having its own page—meaning the specification, engine, and write-back each require one fewer field. Third, the word "step" itself implies precedence, whereas there is no precedence between several ideas belonging under the same idea—precedence only exists via prerequisites. Credit must be given to the first version: the five sentences it wrote have today become the five ideas in the top layer, word for word, without a single change; this is empirical proof that it got half the answer right.
**Why not use the existing section comments in the graph file for grouping?** This was the approach chosen by humans at the start of the first version, but it was rejected after research, and the reasons remain valid today. Comments can be used today—tests show they can be split into ten sections, and the numbers and legends match perfectly. However, they will **silently tell lies**: new ideas created on the web are appended to the end of the file, so every idea created via the web will automatically fall into the last section. This cannot be seen in the change logs or on the page; only the sentence "this section has X ideas" quietly becomes a lie. Two other reasons: comments are a verbal convention, they have never been written in the specification, they do not exist in newly created empty graphs, and if moved to another repository, they become a blank void; furthermore, the library that reads and writes this file format states in its own documentation that its comment handling is not entirely stable. **Rules must be portable; they cannot be built upon something that cannot be carried away.**
**Why set the limit at seven?** A layer exceeding seven lines is not an overview, it is a table of contents—a human cannot scan it in one glance, so they won't scan it. This number can be checked by a machine, so it is a rule, not a suggestion. Fewer than seven is not a complete set, because the few that do make a set tend to become "buckets": this repository itself has produced three ("Known Defects", "Endpoint", "Reading Order"), and they fail to explain "what capability this project gained after completion." Therefore, even that counter-example is written into the specification—if you only write rules and not counter-examples, the next person will make the same mistake.
**Why is a wrong attachment an error, while exceeding seven per layer is only a warning?** Attaching to a non-existent ID, or attaching in a loop, will cause the page to actually lose an idea or fail to render, while the page looks perfectly normal—that is bad, not just unattractive. "This layer has eight" simply means a human cannot scan it in one glance, but the graph itself is still correct; reporting it as an error immediately would cause every repository that has installed this tool to turn red instantly, which would be making others' repositories pay for our new rules. The cost must be stated: warnings are often overlooked, so "maximum seven per layer" currently relies on self-discipline rather than enforcement; once this field has stabilized across various repositories, we will consider tightening it.
**Why does an idea say nothing if it doesn't write its own ownership?** In the first version, this had to be split into two tiers: if steps were declared but an idea had no ownership, a warning would be issued. The cost was that the numbers on the page would be undercounted, and warnings are often overlooked—that was a conscious trade-off. A tree does not have this cost: an idea without written ownership is simply an idea in the top layer, which is a valid state; the page will still display it and include it in the count. Thus, that tier of warning, along with its cost, has disappeared—it wasn't overlooked.
**Why does each idea only write "who I belong to," and not "who belongs to me"?** Storing both directions would result in two sets of potentially contradictory facts, and when contradictions occur, no one knows which one counts. To clarify the weight of this statement: this repository has never actually stored a reverse subordinate list, so this rule is avoiding a problem based on experience elsewhere, rather than fixing a problem that occurred here. The half that can be verified is: by only storing the child-to-parent direction, the parent's subordinate list is recalculated every time. The cost is that retrieving an idea's subordinates requires scanning the entire graph, but with only dozens or hundreds of ideas, this overhead is negligible.
**Why does a complete card for an idea only appear on its own page, with only one line placed on the parent page?** This is not a layout preference, but a mechanism: editing, draft recovery, and human sign-off on the web all find elements in the document by ID. If the same ID appears twice, these processes will silently misidentify one. A single line containing the name, status, and the first line of "what it is" is sufficient to decide whether to click into it.
**"The entire graph is one file" was not a choice this time, but an inheritance.** It is written here because it explains why the page looks the way it does, not because other methods were compared this time: from day one, this web page has been a file that can be double-clicked to open and sent in its entirety to others; write-back, human sign-off, and drafts all find elements by ID within the same document. Therefore, page splitting can only be "all pages are in this one document, hidden first, and then one page is displayed according to its address." The cost must still be noted: rendering seventy-one ideas results in 1.44 million bytes, and it still opens very quickly; if it becomes ten times longer, the math should be recalculated.
**Why is ownership stored as a line of plain text, rather than as a collapsed paragraph like other answers?** It is used for precise comparison with the IDs of other ideas. When a collapsed paragraph is read back, it has an extra newline at the end, making the comparison result always "no one," and this is completely invisible on the page—this is the most expensive kind of error.
**Why are the descriptions of two commands being modified, rather than injecting logic into the program?** A machine cannot determine how to divide a project into major blocks or how to describe each block in plain language; this can only be done by the party that has read the project. What the program can do is validation; what it can write are only descriptions. The reason the description only references that section of the specification and does not copy the rules into it is because this tool has already paid the price for "writing the same thing in three different places" once before—the copied version will inevitably differ from the original, and no one will know which one counts.
**Why is this one idea, rather than three?** The rules, the validation, and the two commands were originally three separate ideas. What actually happened was: the rules were written without validation to support them, the validation was done without the commands following, and all three were describing the same thing. The only effect of splitting them was to make people think that two-thirds of the layering work had already been completed. After merging, according to the rules of the specification, the smallest ID is kept; the other two retain their IDs, are set to blocked, and the record specifies which one they were merged into—IDs are never recycled, and the human sign-off on one of them remains exactly where it was.

**为什么是改那一个标题，而不是每页各印一个**：整份文档只该有一个一级标题，这: **Why change that one title instead of printing one on each page**: The entire document should only have one H1 title; this is consistent with HTML specifications and various accessibility guidelines (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html). Furthermore, the position of the header in the document is **above** the flowchart; printing one on each page would mean they could only be printed below the diagram —— which is not the position you want. **Why the title must change accordingly, instead of letting people look at the cards themselves**: A static title is itself a defect. With 72 pages sharing the same title, a screen reader's title list cannot distinguish between pages; replacing it is fixing an existing bug, not introducing a new risk. **Why the text in the browser tab line is also changed together**: This is the only point explicitly stated by standards —— WCAG 2.4.2, when discussing pages where "content changes dynamically at the same URL," requires the title to change along with the current view (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/page-titled.html). The cost is one line. **Why not "move the focus to the new title after page changes"**: That action is only supported by user research and has no standard requirement (https://www.gatsbyjs.com/blog/2019-07-11-user-testing-accessible-client-routing/); it would require adding tabindex to the title, designing a specific set of focus styles, and distinguishing between the initial opening and subsequent page changes. We are not doing it this time; it remains in "how to use in the future." **Why use the browser's built-in disclosure element instead of writing custom show/hide logic**: Writing it yourself requires handling clicks, states, keyboard interaction, screen reader annotations, and finding ways to ensure in-page search can find collapsed text; the built-in one has all of this, with a cost of zero lines of script, and "collapsed text can still be searched for and automatically expanded" is implemented by all three browser engines (an Interop 2024 completed item, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/491). To be clear about the cost: this behavior cannot be tested in automated testing; it can only be checked manually once. **Why the historical explanation is tucked into the disclosure instead of being deleted**: That passage contains real history (which commit moved the old code, why the numbering restarts from a certain point); if deleted, there would be no other place to record it. It just shouldn't occupy the first screen. **Why the entire block is not output when there is no extra text**: An empty disclosure box would make people think it is broken. This is also the only boundary case in this test that is absolutely indispensable —— without it, an implementation that "always outputs an empty box" could pass all existing rendering tests, because none of the sample images in those tests wrote `overview`.

**为什么复用签字按钮的判断而不是按原文写**：两处判断不一致，就会出现「索引说: **Why reuse the sign-off button's judgment instead of writing it according to the original text**: If the two judgments are inconsistent, it will result in "the index says this needs to be signed, but clicking it leads to a card with no button" — and people will think the page is broken rather than realizing the two judgments are different. Research and testing showed that both currently hit twelve items; it is precisely because they coincidentally match that discrepancies are easier to miss. **Why each row must include an anchor address**: This was found through research — the jump function and the drawing library are in the same module, and the first line of that module is to fetch the drawing library from the web. When a page opened via double-click has no internet, the entire module does not execute, causing all script-based jumps to fail. With an anchor, the browser can jump by itself, though without smooth scrolling or highlighting. This is also why we don't write our own jump set: the existing set is better when it works, and provides a fallback when it doesn't. **Why not place the sign-off button directly on the index row** (the first instinct would be to do this to save a jump): The existing sign-off test uses that marker to find elements in five places; since the index is above the cards, the extra marker would be found first, causing all five assertions to test something else — and they would still remain green. This type of change, where "the test is still green but is no longer testing the original thing," is much more dangerous than a test turning red. **Why the entire block does not appear when the count is zero**: An empty box saying "(0)" would make people click in only to find nothing; whereas the absence of this block itself indicates there are no pending tasks.

"Not yet finished" must be written as "does not equal completed," and **cannot be written as "equals todo"**—if a prerequisite is blocked or ongoing, it also blocks the way, but filtering by "equals todo" will miss it, causing the page to say "no prerequisites are blocking it" when there actually are. When no prerequisites are blocking it, write a clear sentence; do not use that existing dash to represent "none"—the dash reads like "no information" here, whereas we need to state a certain fact.
**为什么和上一个索引共用一套做法而不是各写各的**：两个索引除了判断和行内容之: **Why share the same approach with the previous index instead of writing them separately**: Aside from the predicate and row content, the two indices are exactly the same. Writing them separately would result in two sets of almost verbatim identical code and two sets of almost identical tests, and sooner or later, one would be modified while the other is forgotten. This is also the reason for that prerequisite edge between these two ideas. **Why "not yet finished" must be written as "does not equal completed"**: A pitfall identified during research—if filtering by "equals todo," a blocked prerequisite would be treated as not blocking the way, causing the page to state something contrary to the facts. This type of error will not manifest on today's graph (none of the three ongoing ideas have prerequisites that are not completed), so it can only be caught by tests, not by the naked eye. **Why the phrase "no prerequisites are blocking it" requires careful wording**: The original expected result for this idea was written as "that means it is truly being worked on, not stuck"—actual testing shows this cannot be inferred: among the three ongoing ideas, two have no prerequisites that are not completed, and these two happen to be stuck waiting for human sign-off. Therefore, this sentence can only say "no other ideas are blocking the way," and cannot imply "someone is currently working on it," otherwise the page would be lying about two-thirds of the rows.
