三件事。一，先堵已有的旁路：guard 新增一条对 Bash 的规则——命令文本: Three things. First, block existing bypasses: the guard adds a new rule for Bash—any command text touching .approved, .scan-todo, .applied, graph files or change files, or direct calls to guard.ts must be intercepted, allowing only calls in the form of ideas.ts subcommands; simultaneously, narrow the Bash allowlist in settings from "any npx tsx" to "npx tsx <engine path>". Second, after apply writes to disk, write (pre-write fingerprint, post-write fingerprint, hash of changed files, field-by-field change list) into a ideas/.applied receipt that receives equal protection, and print the field-by-field diff for the human to see. Third, expand approval words: the full sentence "approve <12-digit fingerprint>" only takes effect when Parameter == Current Graph Fingerprint == Post-write Fingerprint in the receipt—after apply, any single change the agent makes to the graph will cause the three to mismatch, automatically invalidating the fast track and reverting to full graph review; if fingerprints do not match, error out immediately and explicitly, rejecting the message, and do not allow silent failure—silent failure will train humans to only paste fingerprints without looking at the content.
对抗审查推翻了原设计的两个假设。其一「agent 造不出批准」现状就是假的：gu: Counter-review overturned two assumptions of the original design. First, the current state of "agent cannot fabricate approval" is false: the guard is only attached to Edit / Write, Bash never goes through it, and the allowlist permits any npx tsx—an agent can just write a script to run it and directly write to .approved. We must block this door first before discussing anything else; blocking this door also closes the known ceiling mentioned in the README about "using Bash to feed fake events to guard.ts." Second, "fingerprint equality = human has seen this graph" does not hold: a fingerprint proves freshness, not source; an agent can sneak in unauthorized changes after apply and then print the real fingerprint—therefore, the fast track must be bound to the protected apply receipt, not just the fingerprint. The boundary of honesty: this mechanism raises the cost of forgery to "must pass through human permission prompts," rather than being mathematically unforgeable. The explicit rejection solution: a headless pipeline feeding "approvals" (claude -p) can be run by any script, which is equivalent to tearing down the door.

For change files with fingerprint mismatches, there is a clear replay path: the agent confirms each change (including the old value) against the new graph with the human one by one; after confirmation, it regenerates the change file with the current fingerprint and then applies it.
交互式斜杠命令而不是 headless 管道：人敲 /ccapply 本身就是真: An interactive slash command rather than a headless pipeline: typing /ccapply itself is a real UserPromptSubmit event, all hooks function as usual, and the approval step remains in human hands. The scope of implementation is limited to the ideas touched by this change; aligning the entire graph is the responsibility of /ccfix—a single submission should not trigger a full repository roam. The division of labor for lightweight modifications is also written into the command: it is faster to simply say a typo correction in the dialogue (since modifying loose text fields allows the agent to use Edit), while the value of the web link lies in batch modifications of loose text and structural changes like adding/deleting nodes and edges.

(1) guard 的 decideOnePath 在 ideas/ 分支加一条: (1) guard's decideOnePath rejects the pattern graph.<agent>.yaml in the ideas/ branch; (2) when striking out, append the sha256 to the read record (append only, without breaking I-055's concurrent fixes), and readWorklist compares the current fingerprint, so if it changes, it is no longer considered read; (3) extract the guard's decision on product files into decideProductWrite and export it from guard, and change the allow command to call it —— add approval and red records to the fixtures for the two CLI tests in I-089, while the assertion semantics (answer allow if writable) remain unchanged.

Each record contains a format version, sequence number, request number, action, session identity, and corresponding content; session registration, messages, read receipts, and subsequent claim changes are all written into the same record stream. Appending and reading snapshots share withProjectLock: uses non-recursive mkdirSync to create a write.lock directory under runtime; if the directory already exists, it performs a bounded wait, defaulting to a maximum of 3 seconds, then returns the holder and a retry prompt; upon success, it records a random owner tag, PID, and timestamp, verifying the tag and releasing it in the finally block. No automatic expiration, no time-based lock deletion; locks left behind by a crash are only explicitly recovered according to the detected owner after all coordination writing processes have stopped; an incomplete owner also requires a shutdown check, with no guessing. Success is only reported after the record is fully written and fsync succeeds. Reading only accepts complete JSON records ending with a newline; incomplete tails left by a crash are discarded by the next lock-holding write, while corruption in the middle of a complete record results in rejection.
The first version recovers state from the record stream every time, with the cost growing linearly with the number of records; a ponytail comment is left in the implementation so that if cumulative messages in a real project make reading latency unacceptable, it can be optimized or migrated to SQLite. inbox is read-only and paginated, returning lastSeq; ack explicitly confirms the delivered sequence number, and the cursor only moves forward and does not skip existing records. Duplicate delivery is allowed when output fails or is unconfirmed; messages are not silently dropped.
Identity, model, and PID are separated; independent sessions use a stable host identifier, while sub-assistants are given additional verifiable sub-identities. The first sentence extraction follows the existing expression in the page (the line summary and page header are identical word-for-word today), first by paragraph boundary and then by period, with abbreviation guards; if it cannot be retrieved, fall back to the previous question, and if still not found, write "this idea has not been clearly written," do not make things up. 调研查了四类现成做法。Jira、Linear、Notion、Backstage: Research investigated four types of existing approaches. Jira, Linear, Notion, and Backstage do not automatically summarize prose; that line must be written by a human—copying it would be equivalent to backfilling a paragraph for each of the eighty-nine ideas, so this was rejected. Documentation generators (Sphinx, rustdoc, Doxygen) do indeed perform first-sentence extraction, but all three treat it as a "fallback for when humans haven't written a summary," and Doxygen has it turned off by default; therefore, we only copy its algorithm (Sphinx's extract_summary is about fifteen lines, including abbreviation guards) and not its status. The third bullet point is handed to calculated facts rather than a summary, a reason derived from the ACL 2023 classification of unfaithfulness in extractive summarization: sentences extracted from prose can distort the original meaning, but facts on a graph will not, because it does not touch the original text at all. The writing style of "2/4," and whether "the count must be specified for direct sub-ideas or the entire subtree," comes from Org mode; "saying it is waiting for 2 unfinished ideas instead of saying there are 3 links" comes from Linear—relationship facts must be filtered by the current status of the other end, otherwise that number is static. Reporting a warning for ultra-long text instead of silent truncation comes from the Clippy approach.

给想法类型加一个可选字段 blocked_because，位置放在 status: Add an optional field blocked_because to the idea type, placed next to the status, not in the line of the eight questions. Only one function must be forced to change: setStatus is the only place in the entire repository where the status of an existing idea is written (covering the three paths of command line, web envelope, and local service); there, judge that "transitioning to blocked must include a reason", passed via --because in the command line; for the path where the behavior field is changed and automatically reverts to blocked, use the existing text and write it directly into the new field. Add one error to check following the "Completed" templates: report if the status is blocked but this sentence is missing, and name which idea it is. On the web, cards use a field (including edit state, escaping, and draft wiring), and expansion rows manually write a pair of labels and values, both placed after the eighth question. Do not expand the plan field list, do not enter the eight questions' wording table, and do not enter questionLines — it shares the approved prompts, and adding a column would hit two assertions; on the command line, it must be printed under the eight questions, specifically as a single line after the show loop. The reasons for the four existing blocked ideas and the validation rules will be implemented at once: the guard will turn every error from check into "session not allowed to end"; adding rules before backfilling would freeze the session.
网上没有一个跟踪工具原生强制这件事 —— Jira 的 Flagged 是个锁死: No online tracking tool natively enforces this — Jira's Flagged is a locked boolean, and reasons can only be written in optional comments; the request to turn it into a required field has been pending since November 2021 with 59 votes and has not been implemented; Trello's custom fields do not even have conditional requirements. Therefore, there is no product to copy, only two practices from actual usage: enforce it at the moment of status transition rather than enforcing it on static files (Azure DevOps attaches required rules to status changes, and this repository's setStatus is exactly at this position); and conditional validation must include a sentence naming the item, otherwise no one can understand the error. Two suggestions were not adopted: selecting the reason from a fixed category — its benefit is statistics on the recurrence of the same reason, and the four blocked ideas in this repository are not even at that volume; saving a separate blocked start date — that would be a redundant field, as setStatus already automatically tracks a dated modification record, and how long it has been blocked can be calculated from there. Both are explicit postponements, not omissions.
「受阻」从一个状态变成一条说得出理由的记录，往后可以按原因归类、可以把受阻的想法: "Blocked" changes from a status into a record that can state a reason; moving forward, it can be categorized by reason, blocked ideas can be placed at the very top of the page along with their reasons, and when a reason points to another idea, it can be turned into a real link that automatically clears when the target is completed.

每个想法的修改记录今天藏在它自己那张卡片里。要知道最近几天项目在动哪一块，只能一: The modification records for each idea are currently hidden inside its own card. To know which part of the project has been moving in recent days, one can only flip through card by card.
每一页最下面出现一块按时间倒序的改动列表，只含这一页的想法和它的子孙；点一条能到: A modification list in reverse chronological order appears at the bottom of each page, containing only the ideas of this page and its descendants; clicking an item goes to that idea; when there are many items, it does not bloat the page.
在 companion/ideas.ts 的 page 末尾、子想法那一块之后加: Add a collapsible block at the end of the page in companion/ideas.ts, after the sub-ideas section: take the idea of this page itself plus all descendants provided by descendants, merge their modification records into a single timeline, sort them by date from newest to oldest, group them by day, print the date, who modified it, and what was modified for each entry, along with a link to jump back to that idea. No pagination: render everything, tuck the old ones into a default collapsed folding element, write the exact number of hidden items in the title; do not place title elements inside the folding title.
「条目多了怎么办」这一条是调研直接推翻原打算的地方。GitHub 那种「还有 N: The item "What to do if there are too many entries" is where the research directly overturned the original plan. GitHub's "N more items / Load more" approach is to save server round-trips, but here we have a static file and no server at all; community discussion records how that approach breaks in-page search and deep links. Since Chrome M96, collapsed elements automatically expand due to in-page search, text fragment jumping, and anchor navigation — therefore, "rendering everything + putting old items into collapsed elements" neither loses search nor links, and requires zero lines of script. Reverse order with grouping by day, and every aggregated record must be able to link back to its specific sub-idea, comes from the activity streams of GitHub and Google Drive; "Whether to aggregate descendants must be two explicit parameters and cannot be ambiguous" comes from the Drive activity API's practice of splitting "this one" and "this branch" into two parameters — the choice here is that every page aggregates its own descendants and specifies this in the title. The cost is explicitly stated: the same record will be statically copied into every level of its ancestors' pages; the two existing indexes are already paying this cost.
有了这条时间线，「最近谁在动哪一块」不必再问人；将来要按人筛、按日期跳，加的是同: With this timeline, "who has been working on which part lately" no longer needs to be asked of people; in the future, filtering by person or jumping by date will simply be adding a filter within the same block, as the data is already on the page.
子想法没有全部完成，父想法就不许标完成、也不许签字: If sub-ideas are not all completed, the parent idea is not allowed to be marked as completed, nor is it allowed to undergo human sign-off.
给「完成」这道门加一条判定：一个想法只要还有子想法不是完成，它自己就不能被设成完: Add a predicate to the "Completion" gate: as long as a sub-idea of an idea is not completed, the idea itself cannot be set to completed, cannot request human sign-off, and even if a human returns an approval code, it cannot be signed; the sign-off button on the webpage will be grayed out; every instance must clearly state which sub-ideas are still missing.
今天父想法可以在子想法一个都没做完的时候先被标完成、先被签字，那个签名等于没有意: Today, a parent idea can be marked as completed or signed off even when none of its sub-ideas are finished; that signature is equivalent to being meaningless. This rule is currently only written in the manual verification sentences of a few parent ideas themselves — I-121 says "all seven sub-ideas completed", I-124 says "six sub-ideas completed" — those are handwritten prose, no program manages them, and adding a sub-idea turns those sentences into lies.
子想法没做完时，命令行标完成被拒并说出还差哪几个；提签字请求被拒；网页上人工签字: When sub-ideas are unfinished, the command line will reject a completion request and state which ones are missing; sign-off requests will be rejected; the manual sign-off button on the webpage turns gray, with the specific sub-ideas blocking it written next to it; all three locations unlock simultaneously once all sub-ideas are completed; the handwritten "N sub-ideas completed" no longer requires manual counting. The "Complete" on the webpage is not within the scope of this idea — no idea can be changed to completed via the webpage; to achieve completion, one must have valid current GREEN evidence, which can only be done via the command line (D20).
在 companion/ideas.ts 的 setStatus 里，「完成」分: In the setStatus of companion/ideas.ts, after the existing four interceptions in the "Completed" branch, add a fifth: if this idea still has any direct sub-idea that is not completed, reject it and name which ones are missing. The predicate shape mimics needsUnmet verbatim (returning either empty or a sentence naming the items) and relies only on the graph itself (both parent and status are in the graph), because pure unit calls without the project directory also use this function; move the private kidsOf and parentKey from the rendering closure to the module scope for shared use, so "who is whose sub-idea" does not need to be written twice. Block two points on the sign-off side: the manual check prerequisite block in requestApproval blocks sending the approval code, and applyApproval performs one more check before writing the signature — if a sub-idea reverts to unfinished after the approval code is sent, only blocking the first point would allow the signature to be applied via that code. On the webpage, gray out the manual sign-off button instead of hiding it, and write in text who is blocking it; first change this button to call the existing awaitingSignature, otherwise the same thing must be modified in two places; grayed-out buttons do not carry data-sign, so the sign-off panel cannot be opened. Do not touch the "Complete" on the webpage — that gate belongs to D20; no idea can be changed to completed via the webpage. Blocked sub-ideas are counted as "not completed" per the ruling, blocking it in the same way. In FORMAT.md, add one sentence to each of the three places stating "parent is inclusion, not sequence": the completion of a parent idea implies the completion of all its sub-ideas, which is a direct consequence of the inclusion relationship, not a second type of sequential relationship; synchronize the copy stored next to the engine.
调研看过的每个工具都收敛到同一个骨架：状态带一个终态标记，不变量写在那个标记上，: Every tool seen in research converges to the same skeleton: the status carries a terminal state marker, and the invariant is written on that marker, not on a state name called "Completed". What cannot be copied is their failure — Jira and Redmine have completely different architectures but identical user complaints, because both companies implement interception as "control disappearance," making it impossible for users to distinguish between a rule and a defect; therefore, here we gray out instead of hiding, and name the items when rejecting. What is explicitly not copied is "automatically marking sub-ideas as completed when the parent idea is completed": Linear makes this an option that is off by default, and GitHub rejected it directly, reasoning that a parent idea's completion does not imply all sub-ideas are completed, as some sub-ideas might be optional. We only look at direct sub-ideas rather than the entire subtree because once each layer holds its own, the entire tree is automatically established, and rejection can name an idea visible on the current page; the prerequisite for these two being equivalent is that setStatus is the only place in the entire repository where status can be changed, which holds true today. Blocked sub-ideas are not counted as completed because in this format, the destination for "Deprecated" is to retain the number, set it to blocked, and write the reason — that is a record of "this thing was not done," not "this thing was finished"; the cost is explicitly stated: a deprecated sub-idea will continue to block its parent idea; if truly stuck, one must either delete it from the graph or add an "Annulled" status (the more sophisticated approach online is that a sub-idea being annulled satisfies the parent idea, but a parent idea whose sub-ideas are all annulled should be considered annulled rather than completed), but we will not do that now.
这条规矩一落地，几个中间层想法上那种手写的「七个子想法全部完成」「六个子想法全部: Once this rule is implemented, the handwritten "all seven sub-ideas completed" and "six sub-ideas completed" in several intermediate-level ideas can be deleted — no longer requiring manual counting, and they will not become lies if an extra sub-idea is attached. From now on, every intermediate-level idea will automatically carry this gate.

多个仓库共用一个管理网站: Multiple repositories sharing one management website
让人在任何设备上打开一个网址，看到自己所有装了这套工具的仓库的想法图；在那里改想: Allow users to open a URL on any device to see the idea graphs of all their repositories that have this tool installed; modify ideas and approve plans there; after each repository pulls the code, the idea graph files will already contain the new content, requiring no manual YAML editing. Division of labor: the engine in this repository is responsible for each repository's own graph pages, write-backs, approvals, and git commits; the URL, login, and multi-repository index are handled by the portal repository LifeCopilotBeta (specifically the I-009 branch in its idea graph). First, connect both sides on the local machine, then move to a machine that is always on.
仓库多了以后，没有一个地方能总览全部项目、在任何设备上直接管理它们。每个仓库的想: As the number of repositories increases, there is no single place to overview all projects or manage them directly on any device. Each repository's idea graph can only be viewed and modified within that specific machine and directory. What is needed is a common management terminal.
在门户里点进某个仓库的图，把一个想法改成受阻并写上原因，另一处检出的同一个仓库: Click into a graph of a certain repository within the portal and change an idea to blocked while writing the reason; after performing a git pull on another checkout of the same repository, that idea in graph.yaml will already be blocked and the reason will be present. Reply with an approval code on the portal's graph page, which has the same effect as replying in the terminal. Run it through on the local machine first, then repeat it from a mobile phone.
引擎侧三件事在本仓库：I-137 让本地小服务接上 git，I-138 把口令和: Three things on the engine side in this repository: I-137 connect the local small service to git, I-138 move approval codes and receipts into git, I-139 open an approval entry that only recognizes host credentials (including an additional segment for I-105). On the portal side, there is one branch for LifeCopilotBeta's idea graph I-009: starting child processes and proxying (I-010), making the project page the highest level (I-011), login (I-012), forwarding approvals (I-013), and deploying to an always-on machine (I-014). Order of implementation: I-137 → Portal I-010, I-011 → I-138 → I-139 → Portal I-013 → Local endpoint I-142 → Portal I-014, I-015. companion/FORMAT.md add a section "Portal", clearly defining the division of labor and three boundaries: host credentials shall not appear in pages or logs; the identity used for synchronization and approval shall never be a human login; receipts are written only by the engine and shall not be generated or rewritten by the portal.
为什么门户放在 LifeCopilotBeta 而不是让引擎自己长出多仓库索引：: Why place the portal in LifeCopilotBeta instead of letting the engine grow its own multi-repository index: users want to eventually merge into LifeCopilot, which already has graph_repos scanning (lifecopilot/graphs.py:82), the /projects interface (lifecopilot/api.py:274), FastAPI, and a background task running once per minute; if the engine grows another one, it would be redundant. Why not use Plane (research conducted on 2026-09-09): the free tier workspace webhook cannot add request headers, so it cannot wake up GitHub Actions; the prerequisite relationship interface paths differ between the cloud and self-hosted versions, and it did not exist at the end of 2024; squeezing eight questions into the work item description box makes the dependency graph invisible; the mapping table, push, and pull components would all require new code. The always-on machine solution moves the editing, human sign-off, and submission capabilities already completed by serve and graph.html as they are; only the three git commands, one directory move, and one entry point are newly written. Why not use rclone to sync to a cloud drive: it only moves files, has no editing interface, does not produce git commits, and would result in two different truths compared to the version in git.
只读 FORMAT.md「门户」一节，能用自己的话说出引擎和门户各管什么、三条边: Read the "Portal" section of FORMAT.md in read-only mode, and be able to explain in your own words what the engine and portal manage respectively, what the three boundaries are, and why Plane is not used.
任何能起子进程、能代理 HTTP、有自己登录的宿主都能接上同一套引擎：别的网页、: Any host that can start child processes, proxy HTTP, and has its own login can connect to the same engine: other web pages, Discord bots, or corporate intranet portals can do so without changing a single line of the engine.
本地小服务接上 git：起服务前先拉取，写回成功后提交并推送，别的程序能把它当后: Connect the local small service to git: pull before starting the service, and after a successful write-back, commit and push; other programs should be able to start it as a background process.
给 serve 加一个开关：打开时，每次渲染页面前先 git pull，每次写回: Add a switch to serve: when enabled, perform a git pull before every page render, and after every successful write-back, commit and push graph.yaml, log.md, and the receipt directory; if pulling or pushing fails, print the error on the page instead of swallowing it. Simultaneously ensure that serve can be started as a background process by other programs: specify a port, do not open a browser, print its own address and token on the first line of standard output, and exit cleanly.
「各仓库 pull 之后已经更新」的前提是有人替人做了提交和推送。serve 已: The prerequisite "after pulling the repository, it is already updated" assumes someone has performed commits and pushes on behalf of others. Since serve is already the sole place receiving web changes, letting it handle the commit conveniently avoids the need to build another synchronization pipeline. The portal needs to start a serve instance for each repository, so it must act like a background program rather than a window opened by double-clicking.
同一个仓库的两处检出：在一处的 serve 页面上改一个想法并提交，另一处 gi: Two checkouts of the same repository: modify an idea and commit it on the serve page of one checkout, and after a git pull on the other, graph.yaml will already contain the new content, and git log will show one additional commit written by serve; when the switch is off, serve behaves exactly as it does today, running not a single git command.
serve() 多一个选项 gitSync，命令行标志 --git-sync，默: Add an option gitSync to serve(), with the command-line flag --git-sync, disabled by default. When enabled: before rendering GET /, run git pull --ff-only; if it fails, return a plain text 503 page where the body is the git error output; after a POST /changes with confirm and a successful atomicWrite, execute git add ideas/graph.yaml ideas/log.md ideas/approvals (the latter only if it exists), git commit -m "Web write-back N times (serve)", and git push in sequence; if any step fails, do not roll back files, but put the error into the git field of the response and append it to log.md. All three commands run through a small function gitRun(projectDir, args) using execFileSync with a 30-second timeout. The background contract adds nothing new: --port and --no-open already exist, and the first line of standard output is already "Idea graph opened at http://127.0.0.1:端口」"; pin this line during testing so the portal can read the address from it.
为什么放在 serve 而不是 apply：apply 是人手搬改动文件的路，提: Why put it in serve instead of apply: apply is the path for humans to manually move modified files, so it is reasonable for humans to perform commits themselves; serve is the unattended path, so only it needs to commit on behalf of humans. Why --ff-only instead of merging: serve does not resolve conflicts for humans; if a conflict occurs, it stops and reports it, following the same principle as the envelope fingerprint lock (FORMAT.md "The change file" baseDigest). Why execFileSync instead of libraries like simple-git: there are only three commands, and the single-file artifact (D28) should not carry an extra dependency for it. Why disabled by default: the version opened by double-clicking on a local machine should not silently push to the remote. Why not print the token to standard output: the page carries the token back itself, and the portal is a transparent proxy, so it does not need it.
常开机器上每个仓库一个 serve，就是完整的同步管道，不需要 CI，也不需要另: Running one serve instance per repository on an always-on machine constitutes a complete synchronization pipeline, requiring neither CI nor another daemon process.
serve 加 --git-sync：渲染前 git pull --ff-onl: serve adds --git-sync: performs git pull --ff-only before rendering (returns 503 with error on failure), writes back to add/commit/push (on failure, populates response git fields and log.md); gitRun is a small function; four tests including two checkout round-trips and a standard output first-line contract.
批准回执有一份进 git：常开机器上产生的回执，人的电脑 pull 之后也认: One approval receipt enters git: a receipt generated on an always-on machine, which is also recognized by a human's computer after a pull.
今天等待回答的口令和回执都只写在每台机器各自的 ideas/.runtime/，: Today, the approval codes and receipts waiting for answers are only written to each machine's respective ideas/.runtime/, and do not enter git. Move these two items into a git-tracked directory ideas/approvals/ (pending/ for approval codes waiting for answers, receipts/ for receipts); the guard's protection for it is the same as .runtime/: it can only be written by CLI and hooks. Receipts in the old directory .runtime/approvals/ remain valid and are read-only compatible. Test pass/fail evidence is not moved and remains in .runtime/. Update format specification D24 and the "Generated files" list with this entry.
口令在人的电脑上由 request-approval 生成，批准要在常开机器上回: Approval codes are generated on a human's computer by request-approval, approvals must be returned on an always-on machine, and the receipt must return to the human's computer for set doing to see. Only git connects these three places. Approval codes do not enter git, so the always-on machine does not know what is waiting for approval; receipts do not enter git, so the human's computer will never see that approval, making a web approval equivalent to no approval.
在一处检出请批准并提交，另一处 pull 之后能回答那个口令、回执落在 idea: Request approval and commit at one checkout, then after pulling at another location, it can answer that approval code, and the receipt lands in ideas/approvals/receipts/; commit it back, and after the first location pulls, set doing allows the same idea; if the content of that idea is modified and run again, it is rejected as before (the rule that receipts are bound to content remains unchanged); an agent attempting to write any file under ideas/approvals/ is blocked by the guard.
paths() 多一个字段 approvals 指向 ideas/approva: paths() adds one more field, approvals, pointing to ideas/approvals; pendingDir and approvalsDir are changed to point to pending/ and receipts/ under it. When applyApproval looks for an approval code file, it first checks the new directory, then the old .runtime/pending/; validApproval first scans receipts/, then scans the old .runtime/approvals/. decideProductWrite adds ideas/approvals to the "only produced by CLI and hooks" group, with the reasoning text citing D24. The path string for the sentence written into the receipt (signed_off) is changed to the new directory. Do not change GITIGNORE_SEED in install.ts: the new directory is intended to enter git. FORMAT.md: D24 adds a section on implementation status, and the Generated files list adds a line for ideas/approvals/.
为什么口令文件也进 git 而不是只搬回执：常开机器要知道有哪些口令在等人回，而: Why approval codes also enter git instead of only moving receipts: the always-on machine needs to know which approval codes are waiting for a response, and approval code files only contain the stage and content fingerprint; request-approval already prints them in full to the terminal (I-102), so there is no secret. Why not change to deterministic approval codes calculated from content (to avoid moving files): it would change the "one-time, random" semantics of D7/D26, and the scope of impact would be much larger than moving a directory. Why pass/fail evidence remains in .runtime/: it is evidence that this specific machine has run the tests; moving it to another machine would mean it is no longer evidence. Why the old directory is read-only compatible instead of migrated: there are not many existing receipts, and scanning two locations is cheaper than writing a migration.
回执进 git 之后，谁在什么时候批了什么内容，成为仓库历史的一部分，git l: Once receipts enter git, who approved what content and when becomes part of the repository history, which can be audited via git log.
网页批准落地：小服务多一个只认宿主凭证的批准入口，走和终端同一条校验: Web approval implementation: the small service adds an approval entry point that only recognizes host credentials, following the same validation logic as the terminal.
serve 多一个 POST /approve 入口，收人回的那一句「批准 CC: serve adds a POST /approve entry point, receiving the human's response "approve CC-XXXXXXXX" and a host credential; the credential is a random string passed to it via environment variables when the portal starts serve, which does not appear on the page and is not printed in logs. The validation is identical to the terminal (approval code exists, content fingerprint unchanged, used only once); if successful, it writes the receipt to the git-tracked directory. If there is no credential or the credential is incorrect, it is rejected, just like today.
用户要求批准也能在网页上做。I-105 裁的是本地页面分不出人和自动化，但它自己: Users require that approval can also be done on the web. I-105 rules that local pages cannot distinguish between humans and automation, but it itself wrote that the only structurally valid method is an out-of-band second location; the portal login is that second location: only after a person passes the portal login does the portal pass that sentence along with the credential to serve, whereas an agent has neither a login nor a credential. Therefore, this does not overturn I-105, it only adds a clause: forwarding after out-of-band login counts, provided the credential does not appear in the page or logs.
带正确凭证发一句批准，回执落在进 git 的目录，set doing 放行；同一: Sending an approval with the correct credential results in the receipt landing in the git-tracked directory and set doing allowing it; sending the same approval code a second time is rejected; sending without a credential, with an incorrect credential, or after content has been modified is rejected and no receipt is left; the credential cannot be found in the serve page source code or standard output.
serve() 启动时读环境变量 AIDEV_APPROVE_SECRET。没设: When serve() starts, it reads the environment variable AIDEV_APPROVE_SECRET. If not set: POST /approve returns 404, same as having no such entry point today. If set: request body {secret, words}, uses timingSafeEqual to compare the secret; if incorrect, returns 403; if correct, calls applyApproval(projectDir, words, {date, session_id: "serve", turn_id: request sequence}), and returns its result as-is; if it returns ok and gitSync is enabled, it commits ideas/approvals/ according to I-137. The credential does not enter the render output, the console, or log.md; standard output only adds one line: "approval entry enabled". Add a fourth paragraph to the "how" section of I-105: forwarding after out-of-band login counts, subject to three conditions (the credential does not appear in the page or logs; the portal login is not something an agent can obtain; receipts are only written by the engine). FORMAT.md D26 adds a section on implementation status, citing these three points.
为什么凭证走环境变量而不是命令行参数：参数在任务管理器和 ps 里谁都看得见。为: Why use environment variables for credentials instead of command-line arguments: arguments are visible to everyone in Task Manager and ps. Why is it received by serve instead of the portal running the CLI directly: applyApproval must run on the machine where the repository is located, and serve is located there; furthermore, the guard rule blocking agents from accessing local services (I-104) still applies to this entry point. Why not change a single word in the ANSWER regex: the portal forwards the exact original words spoken by the human, and the validation must be identical to the terminal to claim "equivalent effectiveness."
